passage: Dear Rukmini, I have to tell someone. In yesterday's seminar on the water project, everyone looked so certain. Even our professor said the budget looked fine. But I noticed that the maintenance cost was left out of the sheet. I kept my hand down. I thought: they are all clever, they must have counted it, and I would look silly. Afterwards, on the stairs, Meenal said, "Did nobody notice the maintenance line?" and Aakash said, "I did, but I thought I was missing something." Half of us had the same doubt and said nothing! I want to bring it up next week. Wish me courage. — Yamini

qa.q: What was left out of the budget sheet?
qa.a: The maintenance cost was left out of the sheet.

qa.q: Why did Yamini keep a hand down in the seminar?
qa.a: Everyone else looked certain, so Yamini assumed the others knew better and feared looking silly; the feeling was doubt turned into self-silencing.

qa.q: What turning point does Yamini choose after the stairs conversation?
qa.a: Yamini decides to bring the maintenance question up next week, having learned that others held the same doubt.

qa.q: What might Aakash have been thinking when saying "I thought I was missing something"?
qa.a: Aakash probably assumed the group must have a reason and that the doubt showed a gap in Aakash's own understanding, so silence seemed safer than asking.

grounding: A student keeps a reservation private because everyone looks certain, not realising several others are silent for the same reason.

passage: Deepak, it's me, Sunaina. Remember the pitch review last week? The whole room was nodding. The slide said two hundred sign-ups, and I had this tiny voice saying that number looks made up. But everyone looked so sure, even Vikram, who is the sharpest of us. So I decided I was the one who did not understand. I stayed silent and even nodded. After the meeting Rina said in the lift, "I thought the number looked odd too," and then Kunal said, "Me too!" I nearly laughed. Three of us had swallowed the same doubt for an hour. Deepak, I am going to say something at the next one, even if my voice shakes.

qa.q: How many sign-ups did the slide claim?
qa.a: The slide said two hundred sign-ups.

qa.q: Why did Sunaina decide to be silent and even nod in the meeting?
qa.a: Sunaina thought everyone else looked sure, so the doubt must be Sunaina's own misunderstanding; it was self-doubt more than agreement.

qa.q: What choice does Sunaina make at the end of the story?
qa.a: Sunaina decides to say something at the next review even if the voice shakes, having learned that others had the same doubt.

qa.q: What might Kunal have felt when saying "Me too!" in the lift?
qa.a: Kunal probably felt relief and surprise at finding out the doubt was shared, after an hour of holding it alone.

grounding: A student keeps a doubt to themselves because everyone else looks certain, not realising others are silent for the same reason.
